scope: Hosted filtering-proxy compatibility with existing analysis cleanup. Actual local Unix-socket proxy and Docker daemon; no personal VM, remote daemon, native app or installer deployment.

additional_source_evidence: The old proxy discarded ownership after every DELETE, including failed removals.
Authorized names/short IDs were forwarded unchanged, permitting a different container to reuse a tracked name.

implementation: New reusable stdlib-only framework policy restricts cleanup listing to one exact tracked analysis name and its full owned ID.
Authorized container references are canonicalized to the full tracked ID before forwarding. Ambiguous names and short IDs fail closed.

Failed/lost removals retain ownership for later ID-scoped absence checks. Only upstream 204/404 marks an entry retired; retired tombstones evict before live entries under the existing 512-record limit.
The standalone deployment launcher consumes framework policy without importing Nexus SDKs. Compose mounts the same module beside the launcher.
The source example drives ordinary Studio execution/recovery plus fault cases through a disposable private proxy, using a preinstalled immutable image.
verified: Ordinary analysis execution and stopped-container recovery complete through the actual filtering proxy.
A running-container DELETE rejected by Docker retains authority; explicit forced removal succeeds and subsequent recovery confirms absence.
An untracked container reusing a retired name survives proxied forced removal and remains inaccessible to proxied inspect. Original-ID cleanup does not expose it.
After proxy restart, an existing container remains intact and its Studio cleanup record remains unconfirmed; lost proxy authority never becomes false absence.
Wildcard, unscoped, multi-name, extra-filter and unknown-ownership listing requests are rejected. Both current array and legacy boolean-set name encodings work.
Full-ID targeting preserves API version prefixes, attach/start paths and query strings.
Bounded tombstone eviction retains live owners first; ambiguous names/ID prefixes never choose an arbitrary container.
A relocated standalone script/policy pair imports with nexus explicitly unavailable, proving no SDK dependency in the deployment proxy.
The same 196-check gate and four actual proxy drills pass before and after the ownership-class move to framework.

runtime.proxy_socket: Private mode-0600 Unix socket below a temporary mode-0700 directory; upstream is the selected local Docker socket.

migration.proxy_ownership: Still process-local, bounded, without a persistent trust store. Restart or eviction requires operator review of unknown ownership.
migration.deployment: Upgrade both docker_proxy.py and studio_docker_proxy_policy.py. Compose includes the new read-only helper mount; source checkouts load the same framework module directly.
migration.rollback: Stop proxy-backed work before reverting. Earlier proxy denies cleanup listing, drops failed-delete authority and lacks full-ID canonicalization.

quality.ruff: New framework/consumer/acceptance files pass normal rules; changed legacy proxy/tests pass with N818 excluded.
quality.preexisting_lint_exception: Denied public exception triggers N818 in HEAD too, confirmed from /private/tmp/nexus-proxy-before.py. Its name was preserved for compatibility.

pending: Authenticated durable proxy ownership across proxy restart/eviction remains open. Unknown objects require independent operator review; this gate proves fail-closed behavior rather than automatic adoption.
Actual personal HTTPS VM installation/TLS/auth/upgrade/restore and remote/SSH Docker/daemon restart remain unverified.
MCP descendants daemonized outside their SDK group still need stronger supported containment. No process-scanning or unrelated PID killing was added.
Physical voice devices, selected service accounts and native Windows/Linux/frozen/installed acceptance remain separate.
Previously recorded mount-source swap race remains a separate deployment constraint; no broader proxy hardening or privilege claims are made.
release_note: Recorded release manifest is unchanged; absent DMG files were not rebuilt or reverified.
